name: The CedarLoom way
description: Claude Code with the CedarLoom, Ponytail and Matt Pocock plugins and CedarLoom's rules; a hub repository for issues and owner questions; a memory repository; project rules, gates and the dev container command.

settings.auto-memory.title: Auto memory off
settings.auto-memory.description: Claude Code neither writes nor reads its own notes from your sessions, so each session works only from the rules and files you can review; what should last goes into the memory repository (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#auto-memory). Switched off after an apply, its keys stay in your Claude Code settings.json until you remove them.

settings.secret-reads.title: No reads of .env files and login files
settings.secret-reads.description: Claude's file tools, and file commands it recognizes in Bash such as cat, refuse .env files (.env.example too) and the SSH, GitHub CLI and Claude Code login files, so their values stay out of the conversation. A command that reads files without naming them, such as grep -r, still can; the sandbox closes that (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#read-and-edit). Switched off after an apply, its keys stay in your Claude Code settings.json until you remove them.

settings.workflow-writes.title: Ask before Claude's file tools write .github/workflows
settings.workflow-writes.description: Claude's file edits to GitHub Actions workflows prompt in every permission mode, bypass included, as a workflow decides what CI runs with the repository's secrets; an unattended session stops at that prompt. Shell commands such as cp or a redirect are not covered (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#actions-no-mode-auto-approves). Switched off after an apply, its keys stay in your Claude Code settings.json until you remove them.

settings.mcp-servers.title: MCP servers: none approved wholesale by your settings, none with your shell's tokens
settings.mcp-servers.description: Your own settings no longer approve every server of a repository's .mcp.json at once, so each waits for your approval unless a repository you trusted approves it in its own settings. Local MCP servers start with a safe baseline environment plus their own env entry instead of your shell's, so a server gets no token you did not give it; a server that read a token from your shell needs it in its env entry (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#project-server-approvals-and-workspace-trust, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars). Switched off after an apply, its keys stay in your Claude Code settings.json until you remove them.

sandbox.title: Claude Code's sandbox for Bash commands, on this machine
sandbox.description: Commands still ask before they run. Off by default: it runs on macOS, Linux and WSL2 only, Linux needs bubblewrap and socat, and docker, which the dev container command runs, fails inside it (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing).

bypass-off.title: Bypass permissions mode disabled in the projects you apply
bypass-off.description: Claude Code then refuses bypassPermissions mode and rejects --dangerously-skip-permissions in each project you apply the profile to, so every session there keeps its prompts. The switch is this machine's: once on, it goes into every project applied afterwards, Orca's included, and Orca starts its Claude Code workers with that flag, so they cannot run there; it is off by default (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#permissions-disablebypasspermissionsmode). Switched off after an apply, the setting stays: remove permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode from the project's .claude/settings.local.json by hand, as undo of the run stops working once Claude Code itself writes that file.

outside-writes.title: No file writes outside the project, in the projects you apply
outside-writes.description: Claude's Write, Edit and NotebookEdit tools refuse paths outside the working directories in every permission mode, apart from Claude Code's own files such as the scratchpad. Shell commands are not limited (the sandbox does that), the EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree tools go, and it needs Claude Code 2.1.314 or later, so it is off by default. The switch is this machine's: once on, it goes into every project applied afterwards (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#permissions-blockwritesoutsideworkingdirectories). Switched off after an apply, the setting stays: remove permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories from the project's .claude/settings.local.json by hand, as undo of the run stops working once Claude Code itself writes that file.
